scenario: AITA for not helping a woman at walmart | I (male 24) started working at walmart for the summer about a month ago. My job mainly involves working with inventory in the back room and not on the floor with customers, sometimes we get heavy boxes that we need to lift as a part of our regular duties. One of my co-workers is a female (fcw) in her early to mid 30s, physically in good shape and as far as I can tell no physical disabilities. (Fcw) approaches me and asks if I can help her lift a heavy box, I say of course and I walk over to the box with her expecting us to perform a team lift - however we get to the box and as I get to one side of the box expecting her to go to the other she just stands there and watches me. I ask "are you ready?" And she says "yes it just needs to go in that bin" (referencing a metal shelving unit about 4 feet high). I say "ok let's do it" and she responds "it's to heavy for me can you please lift it into the bin?". I respond by saying "I'm more than happy to help anyone if they're having trouble with something, but I'm not going to lift all your heavy boxes for you while you stand there watching me" and (fcw) said "if you're not willing to help me I'll find someone who will" and stormed off. Later on the head guy on our team (not my boss just the guy with most seniority who directs us) walks up to me and said " I just spoke to (fcw), the next time someone asks for help you need to help them, that's part of being a team. I responded by clarifying exactly what happened in case she stretched the truth and finished by saying "we're both paid to do the exact same job and if she cant perform the tasks then she shouldn't have taken the job, I'm not the designated heavy lifter on our team and if you would like to discuss this further we can do it with HR present", and at this point feeling pretty annoyed, it was my turn to storm off. So, was I the asshole in this situation? Because so far it seems like its 2 against 1.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I was the asshole in this situation at Walmart. Let me start by going through what happened step by step to understand my actions and the reactions of others. First, I started working at Walmart for the summer about a month ago. My job is mainly in the back room dealing with inventory, which involves lifting heavy boxes. One of my co-workers is a woman in her early to mid-30s, who seems physically fit and doesn't have any obvious disabilities. She approached me and asked for help lifting a heavy box. I agreed, thinking we'd do a team lift. But when we got to the box, she just stood there watching me instead of helping. I asked if she was ready, and she said it just needed to go into a bin that's about 4 feet high. I offered to help, but she said it was too heavy for her and asked me to lift it into the bin alone. I responded that I'm happy to help if she's having trouble, but I'm not going to lift all her heavy boxes while she stands there. She got upset and stormed off. Later, the head guy on our team, who's not my boss but the most senior person directing us, came to me and said he spoke to her. He told me that the next time someone asks for help, I need to help them because that's part of being a team. I clarified what happened, explaining that she didn't help and just wanted me to do all the work. I also mentioned that both of us are paid to do the same job, and if she can't perform the tasks, she shouldn't have taken the job. I added that I'm not the designated heavy lifter and suggested discussing it further with HR if needed. Feeling annoyed, I stormed off. So, was I the asshole here? It seems like two people are against me: the co-worker and the head guy. But I feel like I was just trying to do my job fairly and not take on extra work that's not my responsibility. Let me think about this from different angles. On one hand, teamwork is important, and helping a co-worker in need can foster a positive work environment. Maybe I should have been more accommodating, even if it meant doing a bit more lifting. On the other hand, I'm not the designated heavy lifter, and both of us are supposed to be doing the same job. It's not fair if I'm consistently doing more work while others stand by. I also need to consider the dynamics of the workplace. The head guy is more senior, so his opinion carries weight. He might be trying to maintain team cohesion, even if it means asking me to do more. But I also have the right to express my concerns and set boundaries. Another thing to think about is the physical aspect. If the box was too heavy for her, maybe she should have asked for help earlier or involved someone else who's designated for heavy lifting. It's possible that she felt uncomfortable asking for help or didn't know how to approach the situation. I also wonder about the broader context of the workplace. Are there established protocols for lifting heavy items? Is there a system in place for when someone needs assistance? If not, maybe the issue is more about communication and roles rather than individual actions. Additionally, my reaction to the head guy's feedback might have contributed to the perception that I was the asshole. Storming off after expressing my frustration could have come across as unprofessional or unwilling to work as a team. In summary, while I feel like I was standing up for myself and maintaining fairness in the workload, others might see my refusal to help as being uncooperative or not a team player. It's a tricky situation because balancing individual responsibilities with team dynamics is important, but so is setting personal boundaries. Maybe the best approach would be to communicate more clearly about my willingness to help within reasonable limits and to discuss the workload distribution with the team or management to find a more equitable solution.
